record.summary: Sets a policy of a 'minimally burdensome' national AI framework and acts against state AI laws until one exists. The Attorney General must set up an AI Litigation Task Force to challenge conflicting state AI laws; Commerce must publish an evaluation identifying 'onerous' ones and bar states with them from BEAD non-deployment funds as far as federal law allows; agencies must assess whether to condition discretionary grants. The FCC is to consider a preemptive federal reporting and disclosure standard, and the FTC must say when state laws requiring changes to truthful AI outputs are preempted. A recommended preemption law must spare state child-safety, AI infrastructure and procurement laws.
record.notes: Signed 11 December 2025 and published in the Federal Register on 16 December 2025 (90 FR 58499). The order gave 30 days for the AI Litigation Task Force and 90 days (to about 11 March 2026) for the Commerce evaluation of state AI laws, the BEAD Policy Notice and the FTC policy statement; the FCC proceeding is due within 90 days of the Commerce evaluation. The Attorney General established the Task Force by memorandum of 9 January 2026, chaired by the Attorney General or a designee with the Associate Attorney General as vice chair. The order cites a new Colorado law banning 'algorithmic discrimination' (SB 24-205, US-CO-01); on 24 April 2026 the Department of Justice moved to intervene in xAI's suit against that law, alleging that it violates the Equal Protection Clause. The FTC's proposed policy statement on the suppression of accuracy in AI systems of 1 July 2026 (US-24) says the order directs the Commission to issue it. The White House's legislative recommendations of March 2026 (US-22) set out the preemption that section 8 asks for.

It confirms the title, EO 14365, the 11 Dec 2025 signature, 90 FR 58499-58501 (FR Doc. 2025-23092) of 16 Dec 2025 and the provisions; the White House text of the order, also stored in this run and now secondary_url, adds the President's name. The implementation notes rest on the Attorney General's memorandum of 9 Jan 2026, the DOJ press release of 24 Apr 2026 and the FTC's proposed policy statement of 1 Jul 2026, all stored in this run; the archiver flagged the DOJ release page for review because its title appears little in the text, but the stored text is the release itself. The earlier notes' statements on the Commerce list (not made public, per secondary sources), the 99-1 Senate vote on the moratorium, H.R. 5388 and the absence of a preemption statute rested on law-firm alerts and Axios and were removed (see open_questions). The summary now states the grant and FCC provisions as the order words them.

judgment.status_reasoning: Signed 11 Dec 2025; an executive order takes effect on signature and this one has no later effective date. No stored text revokes it, and the Attorney General's memo of 9 Jan 2026 and the FTC statement of 1 Jul 2026 act under it. 'In force' stands.
judgment.scope_reasoning: An AI-specific executive order on federal preemption of state AI laws, including disclosure and child-safety carve-outs; in scope with no note.

open_questions: Implementation of sections 4 to 6: whether Commerce has published the evaluation of state AI laws, whether NTIA has issued the BEAD Policy Notice and whether the FCC has opened the proceeding. No official source on them is stored; version 1's notes said, from secondary sources, that the Commerce list had not been made public by April 2026. The statement was removed from the notes.

Version 1's notes also said that no federal preemption statute had been enacted as of October 2026, that the Senate removed a 10-year state AI law moratorium from the 2025 reconciliation bill by 99-1 in July 2025, and that H.R. 5388 (American Artificial Intelligence Leadership and Uniformity Act, introduced 16 Sep 2025) was pending. None of these is in a stored file, and they were removed from the notes.
